_comment: Ad placement and the unit ids behind it. Section 10 of CLAUDE.md said no
ads in v1; that was reversed on the owner's call and this file is where
the reversal is tuned. The application id is NOT here — the SDK reads it
from AndroidManifest.xml and Info.plist before any Dart runs.
Everything below can be switched off without a code change. `enabled`
false anywhere means that format never loads, never shows, and costs
nothing: no widget, no platform call.
_bannerComment: On screen everywhere, on the owner's call.
In a match it is pinned to the TOP, above the coverage bar, and that is
not a style choice. Cards are dragged from the bottom of the battle
screen to deploy, and a banner beside that is an accidental-click
generator — AdMob suspends accounts for invalid traffic, so a bottom
banner there risks the revenue it is meant to earn. In menus nothing is
dragged, so it sits at the bottom above the nav bar.
It takes real layout space rather than floating over the arena. The
arena keeps its 2:3 aspect and simply scales down inside what is left:
section 14 forbids changing the aspect, because every deploy distance in
the game is measured against it, but a smaller board at the same shape
_interstitialComment: Shown when a level starts, on the owner's call.
A match is 90 seconds, so `everyNthStart: 1` is an ad roughly every 90
seconds of play. That is legal — a level start is a natural transition —
but it is aggressive, and the usual outcome is that retention costs more
than the impressions earn. Two dials are here to walk it back without a
rebuild: raise `everyNthStart`, or set `afterMatchInstead` true to move
it to the result screen, which is the same frequency without blocking
the thing the player just pressed.
`minSecondsBetween` is a floor regardless of the count, so quitting and
restarting a level repeatedly cannot chain ads back to back.
`skipFirstSession` keeps the ad off the first level of a launch. It is
now FALSE, on the owner's call — the ask was an ad on every start and
this was suppressing one of them. The argument for it stands and the
flag is kept: an interstitial before anyone has seen the game once is
the single biggest driver of a one-star review, and it is the one
impression that reliably costs more than it earns.
`minSecondsBetween` came down from 45 to 10 for the same reason. At 45
a level finished or quit quickly took the next start's ad with it. Ten
still stops a player who is hammering quit-and-restart from chaining
ads back to back, which is both miserable and something Google will
throttle serving over.
_rewardedComment: Opt-in, and the only format the player chooses to see. Loaded but not
yet offered anywhere: the placements worth having are a chest speed-up
and doubling a level's coins, and both need reward plumbing in
ProfileController rather than just an ad call.
